area_overview: Timezone-aware conversion and user-local time handling: machine local vs user local, TimeZoneInfo, JSON/model binding, date math, DST, and scheduling by wall-clock time.
key_ideas: DateTime.ToLocalTime and ToUniversalTime depend on DateTime.Kind and the machine/OS local timezone.
DateTimeOffset.ToOffset changes the displayed offset representation of the same instant.
An offset is not a full timezone; a real timezone has country/region identity and DST rules.
For real timezone conversion use TimeZoneInfo and keep UTC in storage.
ASP.NET Core JSON/model binding handles ISO 8601 DateTimeOffset/DateOnly/TimeOnly values, but APIs should keep payload conventions explicit.
AddDays/AddMonths on instants and 'same local wall-clock time tomorrow/next month' are different requirements.
For user-local scheduling, convert the current instant into the user's timezone, build an Unspecified local wall-clock DateTime, then ConvertTimeToUtc with that user's TimeZoneInfo.
DateTimeKind.Local with a non-machine timezone can throw or misrepresent intent; use Unspecified for local wall-clock values to be interpreted in an explicit timezone.
IsDaylightSavingTime is useful for inspecting whether a specific local time is in DST, but not for implementing all scheduling policies by hand.
